chapter: Bix, Trumbauer and the Goldkette sidemen
title: Paul Mertz, Jimmy Dorsey and the musicians' reputations
summary: Mertz was a great pianist who did not drink, Jimmy Dorsey was a drinker, and the group are remembered as gentlemen.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Also in that band were Paul Mertz whom you still have some contact with.
Tell me about Paul Mertz, what kind of a musician, what kind of man is he?
Didn't he play great piano. He played great piano Honey.
Tell me about him. What kind of fellow was he? Was he very much like the others?
Yes, he was much like the others except that he didn't.....
How about Jimmy Dorsey? What was he like?
He was cute. All of these guys, their image is that they're all very nice people. That's their image.
Yeah. Well if you see them tonight, if you would run into one, he would treat you like a gentleman.
It's incredible. They all have that reputation 50 years later.
That they're all very nice people.
My mother was very good friends with Jimmy and Tommy Dorsey's mother.
Oh. They lived in Forest Hills. Or somewhere in New York. Doc told me or Norma told me about it, when they were living in New York.
